title: Counit-normalized comparisons for a coherent family of chosen adjunctions
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories [def-nagata-category] in fixed universes and let $I$ be an indexing type in a universe containing the families below. For each $i\in I$, specify functors $F_i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $G_i:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ and an adjunction $F_i\dashv G_i$, meaning bijections $\Phi^i_{M,N}:\operatorname{Hom}(F_iM,N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(M,G_iN)$ natural in both variables. Write $\varepsilon^i_N:F_iG_iN\to N$ for the inverse image of $1_{G_iN}$ under this bijection. Suppose specified natural isomorphisms $\phi_{ji}:F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}F_j$ satisfy $\phi_{ii}=1$ and $\phi_{kj}\circ\phi_{ji}=\phi_{ki}$ for every $i,j,k$.

There exists a unique family of natural isomorphisms $\gamma_{ji}:G_i\xrightarrow{\sim}G_j$ satisfying, for every $i,j$ and $N\in\mathcal D$,
$$\varepsilon^j_N\circ F_j(\gamma_{ji,N})=\varepsilon^i_N\circ\phi_{ji,G_iN}^{-1}.$$
In fact the equation determines each component uniquely among all morphisms $G_iN\to G_jN$. These comparisons are the conjugates [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] $\gamma_{ji}=(\phi_{ji}^{-1})^c$ and obey $\gamma_{ii}=1$, $\gamma_{kj}\circ\gamma_{ji}=\gamma_{ki}$ and $\gamma_{ij}=\gamma_{ji}^{-1}$. They identify the specified adjunction bijections: for every $h:F_iM\to N$,
$$\Phi^j_{M,N}(h\circ\phi_{ji,M}^{-1})=\gamma_{ji,N}\circ\Phi^i_{M,N}(h).$$
No triangulated structure, coproducts, compact generation or existence of new right adjoints is asserted or assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] to each specified $\Phi^i$. This supplies the adjunction with precisely that Hom bijection and unit $\eta^i_M=\Phi^i_{M,F_iM}(1_{F_iM})$; its counit is precisely the specified $\varepsilon^i$. In particular, for $a:F_iM\to N$ and $b:M\to G_iN$ we have $\Phi^i(a)=G_i(a)\circ\eta^i_M$ and $(\Phi^i)^{-1}(b)=\varepsilon^i_N\circ F_i(b)$. Thus all subsequent transpositions refer to the chosen bijections, rather than merely to some adjunction between the same functors.

proof.text:
For every $i,j$ set $\gamma_{ji}=(\phi_{ji}^{-1})^c$, applying [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] with $(L_1,R_1)=(F_i,G_i)$ and $(L_2,R_2)=(F_j,G_j)$. That node gives a natural isomorphism $G_i\to G_j$, since $\phi_{ji}^{-1}$ is a natural isomorphism. Its displayed component formula and the forward Hom formula of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] give
$$\gamma_{ji,N}=G_j(\varepsilon^i_N\circ\phi_{ji,G_iN}^{-1})\circ\eta^j_{G_iN}=\Phi^j_{G_iN,N}(\varepsilon^i_N\circ\phi_{ji,G_iN}^{-1}).$$

source.place: Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), following discussion of adjunction maps; Tag 0B65 (lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints), with the indexed coherence calculation written out.

proof.text:
Apply the inverse bijection $(\Phi^j_{G_iN,N})^{-1}$ to the equality in step 2. Its counit formula [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] gives exactly
$$\varepsilon^j_N\circ F_j(\gamma_{ji,N})=\varepsilon^i_N\circ\phi_{ji,G_iN}^{-1}.$$
If any morphism $u:G_iN\to G_jN$ satisfies this equation, the same formula says $(\Phi^j)^{-1}(u)=(\Phi^j)^{-1}(\gamma_{ji,N})$; injectivity gives $u=\gamma_{ji,N}$. Hence any family satisfying the normalization has all its components equal to this one, which proves uniqueness of the family as well as the stronger componentwise assertion.

source.place: Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), following discussion of adjunction maps; Tag 0B65 (lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints), with the indexed coherence calculation written out.

proof.text:
The identity and composition clauses of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] give
$$\gamma_{ii}=(1_{F_i})^c=1_{G_i},\qquad
\gamma_{kj}\circ\gamma_{ji}=(\phi_{ji}^{-1}\circ\phi_{kj}^{-1})^c=((\phi_{kj}\circ\phi_{ji})^{-1})^c=\gamma_{ki}.$$
Here the middle equality uses the assumed cocycle law. Taking $k=i$ gives $\gamma_{ij}\circ\gamma_{ji}=1_{G_i}$, and interchanging $i,j$ gives the other inverse identity. Thus $\gamma_{ij}=\gamma_{ji}^{-1}$, with all laws for the specified adjunctions.

source.place: Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), following discussion of adjunction maps; Tag 0B65 (lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints), with the indexed coherence calculation written out.

proof.text:
Fix $h:F_iM\to N$ and put $b=\Phi^i_{M,N}(h)$. Using the inverse Hom formula of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], the counit equality of step 3, and naturality of $\phi_{ji}^{-1}$ at $b:M\to G_iN$, we compute
$$(\Phi^j_{M,N})^{-1}(\gamma_{ji,N}\circ b)
=\varepsilon^j_N\circ F_j(\gamma_{ji,N})\circ F_j(b)
=\varepsilon^i_N\circ\phi_{ji,G_iN}^{-1}\circ F_j(b)
=\varepsilon^i_N\circ F_i(b)\circ\phi_{ji,M}^{-1}
=h\circ\phi_{ji,M}^{-1}.$$
Applying $\Phi^j_{M,N}$ proves the claimed compatibility of the specified bijections. The construction uses only the given adjunctions and natural isomorphisms in the fixed universes.

Both cited nodes are Mathlib leaves and their statements give what the steps use. lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection gives the formulas Psi(a)=G(a)∘eta and Psi^{-1}(b)=eps∘F(b), with eps=Psi^{-1}(id), the item's counit. def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate gives the component formula, (tau∘tau')^c=tau'^c∘tau^c, id^c=id and preservation of isomorphisms. In step 3, applying (Phi^j)^{-1} gives the normalization, and injectivity gives uniqueness among all morphisms, not only natural ones. In step 4, the composition order checks out and gives the cocycle, gamma_ii=1 and the inverses. In step 5, naturality of phi^{-1} at b gives the Hom-bijection identity. The elementary flags are justified. Edge cases checked: I empty or a singleton, repeated indices, identical functors with different chosen bijections, empty categories. lean.statement: theorem exists_unique_coherent_right_adjoint_comparisons {C : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁} C] [Category.{v₂} D] {I : Type w} (F : I → C ⥤ D) (G : I → D ⥤ C) (a : ∀ i : I, F i ⊣ G i) (phi : ∀ j i : I, F i ≅ F j) (hphi_id : ∀ i : I, phi i i = Iso.refl (F i)) (hphi_comp : ∀ i j k : I, phi j i ≪≫ phi k j = phi k i) : ∃ gamma : ∀ j i : I, G i ≅ G j, (∀ (i j : I) (N : D), (F j).map ((gamma j i).hom.app N) ≫ (a j).counit.app N = (phi j i).inv.app ((G i).obj N) ≫ (a i).counit.app N) ∧ (∀ gamma' : ∀ j i : I, G i ≅ G j, (∀ (i j : I) (N : D), (F j).map ((gamma' j i).hom.app N) ≫ (a j).counit.app N = (phi j i).inv.app ((G i).obj N) ≫ (a i).counit.app N) → gamma' = gamma) ∧ (∀ (i j : I) (N : D) (b : (G i).obj N ⟶ (G j).obj N), (F j).map b ≫ (a j).counit.app N = (phi j i).inv.app ((G i).obj N) ≫ (a i).counit.app N → b = (gamma j i).hom.app N) ∧ (∀ i j : I, (gamma j i).hom = conjugateEquiv (a i) (a j) (phi j i).inv) ∧ (∀ i : I, gamma i i = Iso.refl (G i)) ∧ (∀ i j k : I, gamma j i ≪≫ gamma k j = gamma k i) ∧ (∀ i j : I, gamma i j = (gamma j i).symm) ∧ (∀ (i j : I) (M : C) (N : D) (h : (F i).obj M ⟶ N), (a j).homEquiv M N ((phi j i).inv.app M ≫ h) = (a i).homEquiv M N h ≫ (gamma j i).hom.app N)
